### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/data (route, 50 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fbe1940d23a6c2fc3c1792d2a1158d537edea324` — the merge of head `401e567b59b667fa057f9437601f03ccb2c0a74d` into base `51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fbe1940d23a6c2fc3c1792d2a1158d537edea324 && git checkout fbe1940d23a6c2fc3c1792d2a1158d537edea324
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c 401e567b59b667fa057f9437601f03ccb2c0a74d && git checkout -B drift-repro 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c && git merge --no-ff 401e567b59b667fa057f9437601f03ccb2c0a74d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:devx#3 · `Head-sha: 401e567b59b667fa057f9437601f03ccb2c0a74d` · 2026-11-07T06:31Z

Reviewed against GitHub at the head above, not against the report's own account.

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, line 1 `Fixes #30982`. A closing-keyword scan of the whole body finds no other card number.
- **Premise, measured:** at origin/main `719a502b`, `driver.ts` had `authorTimeoutMs ?? 15 * 60_000`, and `cycle` / `topolog` appeared 0 times under `src/runner/`. All three defects land in one PR. Triage 6689255560 allowed a split only for a difference in kind, and the report gives none: the defects share the runner and differ in degree.
- **File surface:** `GET /pulls/31096/files` lists 14 paths. 13 fall inside the claim's surface (6702660084). One is outside it, accepted as a declared minimal deviation: `test/export/fixture.ts` (+7), a test double that gains `updateRow` because the `AppHarness` interface requires it. There are 0 paths under `src/schema.ts`, `src/loader.ts` or `docs/qa/scenarios/**` (sibling PR #31091). `check-governed-merges --pr 31096`: NOT governed, 1279 changed lines, ≤ 3000.
- **Changeset:** `skip-changeset` is accepted (`@objectstack/scenarios` is `private: true`).
- **Rulings held:**
  - The cost ruling: `API_BILLING_ENV` / `ApiBillingRefusedError` are untouched, and the driver still spawns the local CLI only.
  - Ruling A: the seed plan reads the card's own namespace-relative `expect.lookups`.
  - Ruling D: "not measured" is a runner and scorecard state. `requiredLookups` reads through the scorer's `artifactToEvalGraph`, and there is no second scorer.
- **Spot reads:**
  - `seed.ts` derives cycles from `expect.lookups` with Tarjan SCCs, not from a hand list.
  - Pass 1 defers only lookups the built schema left optional. Pass 2 is one `PATCH /api/v1/data/{object}/{id}` per row (`app.ts` `updateRow`).
  - `prompts.ts` `dataContract` carries "At least one side of a reference cycle must be optional" whenever the card has a cycle.
  - `authorNotMeasured` returns "author timed out after N min" on `timedOut` and "author turn failed: …" otherwise. Build, seed, Run and iterate all return early on it.
  - The `--author-timeout` default is 60 minutes, and it is refused on a replay driver.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - (1) Defect 2's measured root cause: the build prompt rode argv, and `travel_expense` (162,201 B) and `service_desk` (141,922 B) exceed `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072 B), so the CLI failed to start with `E2BIG`. The PR fixes this by sending the prompt on stdin. That is the same defect, beyond the card's literal "record it" ask. It is pinned against a stand-in CLI only; **not measured against the real `claude` CLI**. The card's Verification section (the epic seat's scratch-mode re-run of the four cards) is where that is proven.
  - (2) A build that makes both sides of a cycle required is still seeded, beside the Build finding, so the record holds the platform's own refusals. The card asks for the finding and does not forbid the seed.
  - (3) `error_max_turns` and `is_error` count as "author turn failed".
- **Gates (check-runs at this head, read 2026-11-07T06:31Z):** 15 success, 18 skipped, 15 still running, 0 failure. Landing waits for every check to be green or an expected skip. Local: 50 of 50 derived families exited 0; package tests 364/364; three ablations each turned red and were restored.
- **Out of scope:** none reported.
- **Landing:** when every check is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. `mcp_calls` 0.
